subject: english-literature
title: Limited or All-Seeing?
welcome_lead: Third person comes in two flavours. Pick the right one.
meta_desc: KS3 English Literature adventure on third-person limited and omniscient.
final_note: You can now tell limited from omniscient narration with examples.

concepts.def: Past, present or future of narration.

walkthroughs.h2: How much can the voice see?
walkthroughs.body_html: A limited narrator follows one mind closely. An omniscient narrator dips in and out of every character's thoughts.
Free indirect speech blends narrator and character voice: 'He hated maths. Why was it always so hard?' — the question feels like his thought, but in 3rd person.
Most novels are past tense. Present tense ('I run, I see') creates immediacy but can feel breathless.
